o: Assign and update the value stored in a variable.
Choose suitable integer, real, string and Boolean values.
Trace a short program and write a working calculation using variables.
c: A variable has a name and stores a value. In books = 8, the equals sign assigns the value 8 to books; it is not an equality comparison.
books = books - 3 first calculates 8 − 3 and then replaces the old value of books with 5. Read the right-hand side before assigning the result.
An integer is a whole number, a real is a number with a fractional part, a string is text in quotes, and a Boolean is true or false. For example 12, 2.5, "Jess" and true.
input() returns text. To calculate with a typed whole number, use age = int(input("Age?")); casting converts valid numeric text to an integer. An invalid entry cannot be converted.
